preamble: Labiodentalization of the voiced dental fricative [ð] to [v], the voiced counterpart of the perceptually driven [θ] > [f] shift. In Cockney, Estuary and other south-eastern English accents and in African American Vernacular English it affects medial and final /ð/ (brother > [ˈbrɐvə]), while word-initial /ð/ in function words usually resists. As a completed, context-free change it is attested in the Siirt dialect of Anatolian Arabic, where all interdentals became labiodentals (*ðahab > vahab 'gold').

examples.note: Medial and final /ð/ is fronted to [v]; the from is the conservative pronunciation with [ð] that Cockney inherited. Word-initial /ð/ in the, that rarely becomes [v].
The band name The Bruvvers spells the same fronting.
The from is the conservative pronunciation with [ð].
Non-initial /ð/ is fronted to [v]; word-initial /ð/ is [ð] or stopped [d] instead.

examples.from: Classical Arabic ḏiʔb 'wolf', ḏubbāna 'fly', kaḏaba 'he lied'
examples.note: All interdentals of the Siirt dialect became labiodentals: *θ > f (fa'lab 'fox'), *ð > v, emphatic *ðˤ > emphatic vˤ.
